# Upyun | Apache Reqsign™

# Upyun

Upyun Storage REST API requests signed with the UPYUN header scheme.

UPYUN header signature (MD5-derived HMAC-SHA1)✓ header signing— query / presign✓ WASM[docs.rs/reqsign-upyun ↗](https://docs.rs/reqsign-upyun)

Signs the method, wire path, Date, and an optional Content-MD5 header; expires\_in is not interpreted. Discovered CLI credentials require the first segment of the request's wire path to exactly equal the CLI session bucket on every signature, including cache hits. This is a local request-target check, not a server-side path-rewrite claim.

## Get started[​](#get-started "Direct link to Get started")

```

cargo add reqsign --features upyun


```

```

use reqsign::upyun::StaticCredentialProvider;

use reqsign::{default_context, upyun};


let ctx = default_context();

let signer = upyun::default_signer(ctx, "bucket")

    .with_credential_provider(StaticCredentialProvider::new("operator", "password"));


// Build the request and choose the bucket endpoint in the caller.

let mut req = http::Request::put("https://v0.api.upyun.com/bucket/object.txt")

    .body(())?

    .into_parts()

    .0;


signer.sign(&mut req, None).await?;


```

The default chain selects the session for `bucket` from the Upyun CLI (`upx`) configuration at `~/.upx.cfg`. A matching current session is preferred, then the first session for that bucket. The discovered credential is scoped to that bucket: every signature requires the first segment of the request's wire path to exactly equal it, including when a cached credential is reused. This is a local check of the request target and does not assume server-side path rewriting. The file has no account or endpoint scope beyond the bucket. Install`StaticCredentialProvider` directly, or push it in front of the default chain, when credentials come from application configuration; explicit static credentials are unscoped unless the caller sets a bucket. The default source and prepended providers fail closed: a provider error is returned instead of falling through to a lower-priority source.

The signer adds `Date` and `Authorization`. Set `Content-MD5` before signing when the request body should participate in the signature. The signed URI is the request's wire path and raw query exactly as supplied, so endpoints such as`?usage` and `?metadata=...` are covered; the signer does not decode, reorder, or rebuild those bytes. It does not create presigned URLs or token credentials, and it does not send the request.

## Credentials

### Default credential chain

The default signer tries these sources in order and uses the first one that yields a credential — no configuration needed when any of them is present:

1. Upyun CLI (upx) configuration (\~/.upx.cfg, bucket-scoped)

### Credential providers

Available `ProvideCredential` implementations. Construct any of them directly, reorder them, or compose them into your own chain — see [Loading credentials](/docs/guides/credentials/):

* [UpxConfigCredentialProvider](https://docs.rs/reqsign-upyun/latest/reqsign%5Fupyun/struct.UpxConfigCredentialProvider.html) — Upyun CLI (upx) configuration (\~/.upx.cfg, bucket-scoped)
* [StaticCredentialProvider](https://docs.rs/reqsign-upyun/latest/reqsign%5Fupyun/struct.StaticCredentialProvider.html) — Static operator and password

# Vercel Artifacts | Apache Reqsign™

# Vercel Artifacts

Vercel Artifacts API requests at https://api.vercel.com/v8/artifacts authenticated with a bearer token. The cache key, team or owner scope query, endpoint, and artifact headers stay with the caller.

Bearer token✓ header signing— query / presign✓ WASM[docs.rs/reqsign-vercel ↗](https://docs.rs/reqsign-vercel)

Inserts a sensitive Authorization: Bearer header and leaves the URI and every other header unchanged; expires\_in is rejected because the Vercel Remote Cache API has no query authentication.

## Get started[​](#get-started "Direct link to Get started")

```

cargo add reqsign --features vercel


```

```

use reqsign::{default_context, vercel};


// TURBO_TOKEN, then VERCEL_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN — resolved by the default chain.

let ctx = default_context();

let signer = vercel::default_artifacts_signer(ctx);


let mut req = http::Request::builder()

    .method(http::Method::PUT)

    .uri("https://api.vercel.com/v8/artifacts/example-hash?teamId=team_example")

    .body(())?

    .into_parts()

    .0;


// Sign in place, then send with the HTTP client you already use.

signer.sign(&mut req, None).await?;


```

The signer inserts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which is how the Vercel Artifacts API authenticates Remote Cache calls.

## Credential discovery[​](#credential-discovery "Direct link to Credential discovery")

The default chain reads:

1. `TURBO_TOKEN` through `Context` environment access. Turborepo documents it as the bearer token for Remote Cache access.
2. `VERCEL_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN` through `Context` environment access. Vercel injects it into its build environments.

When both are present, `TURBO_TOKEN` is tried first; the Vercel-injected variable is the build-environment fallback. Vercel's OIDC token exchange for CI produces a short-lived Turborepo access token; Reqsign accepts that token but does not perform the exchange.

`TURBO_TEAM`, `TURBO_TEAMID`, and `VERCEL_ARTIFACTS_OWNER` are not read. They describe the cache scope rather than the identity, so the caller adds them as the`teamId` or `slug` query parameter.

A present but unusable token, or an invalid prepended or static provider, fails signing instead of silently selecting a different identity. An absent token yields no credential, and signing then reports `CredentialInvalid`.

## Cache key and scope stay with the caller[​](#cache-key-and-scope-stay-with-the-caller "Direct link to Cache key and scope stay with the caller")

The signer preserves the URI. The caller chooses the API endpoint, the cache key in `/v8/artifacts/<hash>`, the team or owner scope query, and artifact headers such as `x-artifact-duration`.

The default API host is `https://api.vercel.com`; self-hosted Remote Cache implementations and a caller-selected endpoint remain outside Reqsign.

## Request behavior[​](#request-behavior "Direct link to Request behavior")

`ArtifactsRequestSigner` inserts a sensitive `Authorization` header and leaves the URI and every other header unchanged. The Vercel Remote Cache API has no query authentication, so signing rejects `expires_in`.

A token is long-lived or refreshed by the caller's CI flow. It carries no expiry that Reqsign can read, and signing writes no protocol time, so signing has no clock dependency. Refresh or rotate it with the mechanism your deployment already uses; an expired token fails at the API.

The caller owns the HTTP client and its redirect policy. Do not forward the signed `Authorization` header to a different host.

## WASM[​](#wasm "Direct link to WASM")

Environment and static credentials plus header signing work on`wasm32-unknown-unknown` without a JavaScript clock.

## Credentials

### Default credential chain

The default signer tries these sources in order and uses the first one that yields a credential — no configuration needed when any of them is present:

1. TURBO\_TOKEN
2. VERCEL\_ARTIFACTS\_TOKEN injected by Vercel

### Credential providers

Available `ProvideCredential` implementations. Construct any of them directly, reorder them, or compose them into your own chain — see [Loading credentials](/docs/guides/credentials/):

* [ArtifactsEnvCredentialProvider](https://docs.rs/reqsign-vercel/latest/reqsign%5Fvercel/struct.ArtifactsEnvCredentialProvider.html) — TURBO\_TOKEN
* [ArtifactsVercelEnvCredentialProvider](https://docs.rs/reqsign-vercel/latest/reqsign%5Fvercel/struct.ArtifactsVercelEnvCredentialProvider.html) — VERCEL\_ARTIFACTS\_TOKEN injected by Vercel
* [ArtifactsStaticCredentialProvider](https://docs.rs/reqsign-vercel/latest/reqsign%5Fvercel/struct.ArtifactsStaticCredentialProvider.html) — Static Vercel Artifacts bearer token

# Vercel Blob | Apache Reqsign™

# Vercel Blob

Vercel Blob API requests authenticated with a read-write token. The endpoint, pathname, access level, upload options, and Blob API headers stay with the caller.

Bearer token✓ header signing— query / presign✓ WASM[docs.rs/reqsign-vercel ↗](https://docs.rs/reqsign-vercel)

Inserts a sensitive Authorization: Bearer header and leaves the URI and every other header unchanged; expires\_in is rejected because Vercel Blob has no query authentication.

## Get started[​](#get-started "Direct link to Get started")

```

cargo add reqsign --features vercel


```

```

use reqsign::{default_context, vercel};


// BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN — resolved by the default chain.

let ctx = default_context();

let signer = vercel::default_blob_signer(ctx);


let mut req = http::Request::builder()

    .method(http::Method::PUT)

    .uri("https://vercel.com/api/blob/reports/2026%20Q1.csv?addRandomSuffix=0")

    .body(())?

    .into_parts()

    .0;


// Sign in place, then send with the HTTP client you already use.

signer.sign(&mut req, None).await?;


```

The signer inserts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which is how a Vercel Blob read-write token authenticates Blob API calls.

## Credential discovery[​](#credential-discovery "Direct link to Credential discovery")

The default chain reads `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` through `Context` environment access. Vercel documents this variable as the long-lived static read-write token for code running outside Vercel.

Vercel's OIDC flow (`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` with `BLOB_STORE_ID`) and client-token flows need store or operation context in the request, so they are not part of the default chain. Pass a caller-managed token through`BlobStaticCredentialProvider` when the application already owns one.

A present but unusable `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, or an invalid prepended or static provider, fails signing instead of silently selecting a different identity. An absent token yields no credential, and signing then reports `CredentialInvalid`.

## Endpoint and request fields stay with the caller[​](#endpoint-and-request-fields-stay-with-the-caller "Direct link to Endpoint and request fields stay with the caller")

The signer preserves the URI. The caller chooses the Blob API endpoint, pathname, method, access level, upload options, and headers such as `x-api-version`. Vercel's current SDK targets `https://vercel.com/api/blob` for control-plane calls and serves blob content from `*.blob.vercel-storage.com`; a custom or emulator endpoint remains a caller choice.

The token is scoped to a Blob store, but the request pathname and access level select the object or upload behavior. Reqsign does not build those fields.

## Request behavior[​](#request-behavior "Direct link to Request behavior")

`BlobRequestSigner` inserts a sensitive `Authorization` header and leaves the URI and every other header unchanged. The Blob API has no query authentication, so signing rejects `expires_in`.

A read-write token is long-lived and carries no expiry that Reqsign can read. Signing writes no protocol time, so signing has no clock dependency. Rotate the token with the mechanism your deployment already uses; a revoked token fails at the API.

The caller owns the HTTP client and its redirect policy. Do not forward the signed `Authorization` header to a different host.

## WASM[​](#wasm "Direct link to WASM")

Environment and static credentials plus header signing work on`wasm32-unknown-unknown` without a JavaScript clock.

The default signer tries these sources in order and uses the first one that yields a credential — no configuration needed when any of them is present:

1. BLOB\_READ\_WRITE\_TOKEN

# Yandex Disk | Apache Reqsign™

# Yandex Disk

Yandex Disk REST API requests to cloud-api.yandex.net authenticated with an OAuth access token. The API version, resource path, query parameters, upload or download URLs, and storage parameters stay with the caller.

OAuth access token✓ header signing— query / presign✓ WASM[docs.rs/reqsign-yandex-disk ↗](https://docs.rs/reqsign-yandex-disk)

Inserts a sensitive Authorization: OAuth header and leaves the URI and every other header unchanged; expires\_in is rejected because Yandex Disk has no query authentication.

## Get started[​](#get-started "Direct link to Get started")

```

cargo add reqsign --features yandex-disk


```

```

use reqsign::{default_context, yandex_disk};


// Yandex Disk has no documented automatic token source.

let ctx = default_context();

let signer = yandex_disk::default_signer(ctx, "yandex-disk-oauth-token");


let mut req = http::Request::get(

    "https://cloud-api.yandex.net/v1/disk/resources?path=disk%3A%2Ffolder%2Ffile",

)

.body(())

.unwrap()

.into_parts()

.0;


// Adds Authorization: OAuth <token> and leaves the URI unchanged.

signer.sign(&mut req, None).await?;


```

The [Yandex Disk REST API](https://yandex.ru/dev/yandex-360/disk/rest/en/concepts/quickstart)authenticates requests with `Authorization: OAuth <access token>`. The token is issued by Yandex OAuth to an app for a specific user's Disk.

Yandex documents no environment variable, CLI token store, or well-known credential file for these tokens, so Reqsign does not infer one.`default_signer` therefore takes the token explicitly, and`DefaultCredentialProvider::new()` has an empty automatic chain. Compose`StaticCredentialProvider` with `push_front`, or supply a dynamic`ProvideCredential` when the token rotates:

```

use reqsign::{Context, Signer};

use reqsign::yandex_disk::{RequestSigner, StaticCredentialProvider};


let provider = StaticCredentialProvider::new("yandex-disk-oauth-token");

let signer = Signer::new(ctx, provider, RequestSigner);


```

Token issuance, refresh, revocation, and the permissions attached to the OAuth app stay with the caller. Reqsign does not implement authorization-code, device, or interactive flows. A static token without an expiry is cached for the signer's lifetime; use `StaticCredentialProvider::with_expires_at` when the token has a known fixed lifetime, or a dynamic `ProvideCredential` that returns a fresh credential with an expiry when the token rotates.

## Request ownership[​](#request-ownership "Direct link to Request ownership")

The caller owns the API host, API version, resource path, query parameters,`Accept` and `Content-Type` headers, and any upload or download URL returned by Yandex Disk. The signer inserts a sensitive `Authorization` header and preserves the URI and every other header. There is no query authentication, so signing rejects `expires_in`.

## Credentials

### Default credential chain

This provider has no ambient default source. Supply an explicit credential provider as described on this page.

### Credential providers

Available `ProvideCredential` implementations. Construct any of them directly, reorder them, or compose them into your own chain — see [Loading credentials](/docs/guides/credentials/):

* [StaticCredentialProvider](https://docs.rs/reqsign-yandex-disk/latest/reqsign%5Fyandex%5Fdisk/struct.StaticCredentialProvider.html) — Static Yandex Disk OAuth access token

# Signing contracts | Apache Reqsign™

# Signing contracts

Reqsign's behavior at the edges is specified, not incidental. This page is the reference for the six contracts `sign` and `grant` uphold; each is backed by the API documentation in `reqsign-core` and exercised by tests.

## Wire-ready URIs[​](#wire-ready-uris "Direct link to Wire-ready URIs")

**The contract:** `sign` takes a _wire-ready_ request head. The URI you pass is the URI that goes on the wire — built-in signers require an authority and expect path and query data to be **percent-encoded exactly once** before the call. Signing does not perform general-purpose URI encoding for the caller.

Signature protocols canonicalize the URI (SigV4 builds its canonical request from the encoded path and sorted query). If the signer re-encoded your input, an already-encoded `%2F` would double-encode while a raw space got "helpfully" fixed — and the signed bytes would depend on who encoded last. Exactly-once encoding, owned by the caller, removes the ambiguity: what you signed is what you send.

Swift TempURL is a provider-specific exception. Its separate `presign` entry point keeps the caller's encoded path and query bytes in the outgoing URI, but uses the path after one percent-decoding step for the HMAC input, matching the decoded request path Swift verifies.

```

// Object key: "reports/2026 Q1.csv" — encode once when building the URI:

let uri = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/my-bucket/reports/2026%20Q1.csv";


```

Rules of thumb: encode path segments and query values once, when constructing the URI; never pass a decoded "pretty" URI expecting a fix-up; never re-encode after signing (for presigned URLs this breaks the signature); relative URIs are not signable. Some service crates export percent-encoding helpers tuned to their provider's canonicalization (for example `reqsign-volcengine-tos`'s `percent_encode_path`).

## Atomic request mutation[​](#atomic-request-mutation "Direct link to Atomic request mutation")

**The contract:** if credential loading or request signing returns an error, the request is **unchanged**. On success, only `req.uri` and `req.headers`may change; the method, version, and extensions retain their input values.

```

match signer.sign(&mut req, None).await {

    Ok(()) => { /* req is signed: uri and/or headers updated, nothing else */ }

    Err(e) => { /* req is byte-for-byte what you built */ }

}


```

Without atomicity, an error path could leave a half-signed request — an`Authorization` header from one attempt, query parameters from another — forcing callers to rebuild requests defensively around every failure. With it: retries reuse the original request as-is, fallback signing is safe, and a request never carries remnants of a signature that was not fully produced. The guarantee covers the request head; bodies are never touched.

## Credential freshness[​](#credential-freshness "Direct link to Credential freshness")

**The contract:** a cached credential is reused only when it is fresh according to `SigningCredential::is_valid` **and** usable through the operation's deadline (`required_valid_until`). A freshly loaded credential only needs to satisfy the exact operation deadline. Provider errors are returned without internal retry and without falling back to the previously cached credential.

The two validity checks have different jobs — `is_valid()` answers the_caching_ question and may include a proactive refresh window;`is_valid_at(ts)` answers the _operation_ question with no buffers (see[Architecture](/docs/architecture/#credential-caching-and-validity)). Deadlines come from the operation: essentially "now" for header signing, the full window for a presigned URL — so a credential expiring in five minutes triggers a refresh rather than producing a URL that dies early.

## Expiration semantics[​](#expiration-semantics "Direct link to Expiration semantics")

**The contract:** `expires_in` is a _service-specific validity input_. It does not universally select query authentication — the configured service signer and credential type determine how the duration is interpreted.

| Interpretation                                         | Providers                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Selects query authentication with that validity window | AWS SigV4/SigV4a, Aliyun OSS, Tencent COS, Volcengine TOS, Google Cloud Storage (V4 signed URLs), Huawei Cloud OBS |
| Bounds credential validity; header signing regardless  | Oracle Cloud                                                                                                       |
| Ignored; header signing always uses the current Date   | Upyun                                                                                                              |
| Rejected; header authentication only                   | Aliyun Drive, Cloudflare, Yandex Disk                                                                              |
| Rejected; static query authentication only             | Baidu Netdisk                                                                                                      |
| Rejected; header signing only                          | Vercel Blob, Vercel Artifacts                                                                                      |
| Requests a granted credential's validity window        | Granting operations (subject to the operation's own maximum)                                                       |

Whatever the provider does with it, one obligation is universal: the credential used must remain usable for the full window — the signer refreshes or errors rather than producing an artifact that dies early. And three things it never means: it never _shortens_ a credential's own lifetime; it never overrides a provider-side maximum (S3 presign caps at 7 days — exceeding a cap is a provider-side error, not silent truncation); and `None` never means "no expiry" for the artifact (header signatures still embed timestamps with provider-defined validity).

## Secret redaction[​](#secret-redaction "Direct link to Secret redaction")

**The contract:** formatting Reqsign types with `Debug` does not reveal secret material. Credential types implement `Debug` by hand, wrapping sensitive fields in a `Redact` helper; composite types like `Signer` print structure, not contents. Non-sensitive metadata (like expiration) prints normally so logs stay useful.

```

log::debug!("loaded: {credential:?}");

// Credential { access_key_id: Redacted, secret_access_key: Redacted, ... }


```

Redaction covers _accidental_ leaks — `{:?}` in a log line, a panic message, an error chain. It cannot protect secrets you extract on purpose: accessor methods return real values, and a signed request's `Authorization` header or presigned URI **contains derived authentication material** — log a presigned URI and you have logged a usable capability. Redact at your logging layer, and give custom `ProvideCredential` implementations a manual `Debug` over redacted fields too. Report suspected leaks through the[ASF security process](https://www.apache.org/security/), never the public issue tracker.

## Errors and retries[​](#errors-and-retries "Direct link to Errors and retries")

**The contract:** The signer and granter propagate errors returned by their configured provider; you own retries. `sign` and`grant` perform no internal retries, no fallback signers, and no silent reuse of stale credentials. Combined with atomic mutation, any error leaves the request head unchanged — free to retry, reroute, or fail. This does not prevent a `ProvideCredentialChain` from trying later sources after individual provider errors; see [Loading credentials](/docs/guides/credentials/).

`reqsign_core::Error` carries an `ErrorKind` designed for retry decisions:

| Kind              | Meaning                                  | Sensible default                |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| CredentialInvalid | Credential missing, expired, or unusable | Refresh source, then retry      |
| PermissionDenied  | Authenticated but not authorized         | Do not retry                    |
| ConfigInvalid     | Malformed profile/config input           | Fix configuration; do not retry |
| RequestInvalid    | The request cannot be signed as given    | Fix the request; do not retry   |
| RateLimited       | A credential endpoint throttled us       | Retry with backoff              |
| Unexpected        | Transient or unclassified failure        | Retry with backoff, bounded     |

Errors preserve their source chain (`std::error::Error::source`), so transport details from a metadata fetch or STS exchange stay inspectable.

Why no built-in retry: Reqsign sits _inside_ clients that already have retry policies — an HTTP middleware, a storage layer, a job runner. A second, inner retry loop multiplies attempts invisibly and turns rate limits into storms. Most callers simply propagate signing errors to the layer that already retries requests.

---

url: https://reqsign.apache.org/docs/reference/versioning-and-targets/
---
# Versioning and targets | Apache Reqsign™

# Versioning and targets

## Versioning[​](#versioning "Direct link to Versioning")

Reqsign publishes many crates on five tracks:

| Track                       | Crates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Scheme                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Core + established services | reqsign-core, reqsign-aws-core, every established reqsign-<provider> service crate, reqsign-http-message-signatures, reqsign-file-read-tokio, reqsign-command-execute-tokio                                                                                                             | Lockstep major (currently 4.x)                                                                                 |
| Provider and shared crates  | reqsign-b2, reqsign-aliyun-drive, reqsign-baidu-netdisk, reqsign-cloudflare, reqsign-dropbox, reqsign-github, reqsign-koofr, reqsign-oauth2, reqsign-onedrive, reqsign-seafile, reqsign-upyun, reqsign-vercel, reqsign-yandex-disk, and later crates introduced after the lockstep line | Independent major, starting at 1.0.0                                                                           |
| Crypto backends             | reqsign-crypto-rustcrypto, reqsign-crypto-boring                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Independent major, starting at 1.0.0                                                                           |
| Reqwest adapter             | reqsign-http-send-reqwest                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Independent major (currently 5.x), offset from the core major so reqwest major bumps do not force a core major |
| Facade                      | reqsign                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Independent (currently 0.21.x)                                                                                 |

Lockstep means any `4.x` established service crate composes with any `4.x`core. Provider and shared crates start at `1.0.0` and depend on the current core major, so a `1.x` crate composes with `4.x` core. Crypto backends version independently of both, and the reqwest adapter moves to a new major when the core lockstep major changes, one major ahead. Mixing core majors fails to compile — the trait definitions are the compatibility boundary, and Cargo enforces it.

Applications should depend on the facade and let it pin compatible components; libraries should depend on `reqsign-core` plus their service crates with major-only bounds, leaving context implementations to the application:

```

# Application:

reqsign = { version = "0.21", features = ["aws"] }


# Library:

reqsign-core = "4"

reqsign-aws-v4 = "4"


```

Every release ships as an ASF source release plus crates.io packages — see[Download](/download/). Release notes and migration steps for breaking majors are published with each[GitHub release](https://github.com/apache/reqsign/releases).

## Targets[​](#targets "Direct link to Targets")

**Rust version.** The workspace declares `rust-version = "1.87.0"` — the minimum supported Rust. The RustCrypto backend's `rsa 0.10` dependency requires this version. CI tracks stable; MSRV bumps are treated as observable changes, not patch-level noise.

**Native.** Reqsign is pure Rust with no C dependencies of its own; CI exercises Linux, macOS, and Windows. The default context components (Tokio file reading and command execution, reqwest HTTP) run wherever those crates do.

**WASM.** `wasm32-unknown-unknown` is a supported, CI-verified target for a defined subset: `reqsign-core`, `reqsign-aws-core`, and the AWS SigV4, AWS SigV4a, Azure Storage, GitHub, Aliyun OSS, Aliyun Drive, Backblaze B2, Baidu Netdisk, Cloudflare, Vercel Blob, Vercel Artifacts, Tencent COS, Dropbox, HTTP Message Signatures, Koofr, OneDrive, Upyun, Yandex Disk, and Seafile providers. The shared`reqsign-oauth2` crate and the `oauth2` facade feature are checked in the same subset. Cloudflare and Vercel environment, static, and header signing work without a JavaScript clock. Baidu Netdisk static query signing needs no JavaScript clock. Seafile signing also needs no JavaScript clock. Koofr signing needs no JavaScript clock. GitHub environment, static, and anonymous signing work without a JavaScript clock; GitHub CLI discovery needs a`CommandExecute` adapter and is unavailable in bare WASM runtimes. Yandex Disk static credentials without an expiry and header signing work without a JavaScript clock; expiring Yandex Disk credentials read it. B2 signing and the Upyun default signer, HTTP Message Signatures signing, expiring Yandex Disk credentials, and Dropbox, OAuth2, Aliyun Drive, and OneDrive runtime signing or refresh require a wasm-bindgen JavaScript host for the clock; see the[Custom runtimes & WASM guide](/docs/guides/custom-runtimes/). The clock-free and clock-dependent examples in this page are not exhaustive: a compile-tested provider not named here may still read the clock on some runtime paths. The[provider matrix](/docs/providers/) is the authoritative per-provider status.

**Async runtimes.** `reqsign-core` is runtime-agnostic — nothing in core assumes Tokio. Runtime coupling lives only in the optional context crates; swap them to run elsewhere.
